Rule 301(b)(1) states the aggregate indebtedness leg two ways: 6 2/3% of aggregate indebtedness, and 'aggregate indebtedness cannot exceed 1500% of net capital'. The table holds the 1500% ceiling because it is exact in decimal; 6 2/3% is not.
Amendment A5 to ORDER SC-3 (approved by Bill on 5 October 2026) replaced the membership page's single $10,000,000 criterion with Rule 301(b)(1)'s greater-of.

The procedure states the wheel algorithm itself; ORDER SC-3 amendment A1 (approved by Bill on 5 October 2026) implements that algorithm in code and holds its figures here.

source.verbatim: Every Clearing Member that is a fully-registered broker-dealer must maintain minimum net capital equal to the greater of: (i) $10 million;

(ii) in the case of a broker -dealer not electing to operate pursuant to the alternative net capital requirements, 6 2/3% of its aggregate indebtedness (i.e., aggregate indebtedness cannot exceed 1500% of net capital);
(iii) in the case of a broker-dealer electing to operate pursuant to the alternative net capital requirements, 2% of its aggregate debit items.
If the number of exercised contracts is less than the number of contracts held in open short positions, exercises are assigned in standard assignment increments of 25 contracts.
T1 = S/I (with decimals carried to six places; T1 is rounded up so that it is an integer)
